title: Phased Rollout Orchestration: Wave Planner & Failure-Mode Recipes for Runtime, Console, and API
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive, rehearsable playbook and tooling config for phased multi-surface rollouts (runtime, console, API) that minimizes blast radius while enabling predictable throughput and latency SLAs. Scope includes wave-sizing guidance, canary traffic split templates, automated SLO gates (latency, error-rate, QPS), capacity reservation signals, rollback decision trees, communications templates, and required infra hooks (feature-flagging, model-pin metadata, and routing policy overrides). Deliverables: (1) Wave Planner spreadsheet with macros for capacity + expected token throughput by wave; (2) Failure-Mode Recipes doc with measurable rollback triggers and mitigation scripts; (3) Canary config templates (traffic %, duration, metric thresholds) for the release conductor; (4) Runbook for post-cutover health checks and escalations; (5) RFC for automation hooks required from Eng (routing-policy API, emergency fallback toggle). Success criteria: playbook used for at least one runtime+console+API release with zero customer-facing outage and <10% rollback-required waves, and post-mortem shows runbook was followed. Stakeholders: Product (Daisy Chen), Runtime Eng (lead: Rajiv Sharma), Console Eng (lead: Lena Cho), SRE (Hannah Kim), Solutions & Customer Success (James O'Leary).
updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with stakeholders; aligned on objective and scope. Agreed to target a single canonical playbook that can be parameterized per-market and per-customer tier.

2026-03-03: Draft Wave Planner spreadsheet created (link below). Initial template assumes 4 waves: canary (1%), small cohort (5%), regional ramp (25%), global (69%). Need engineering input on safe canary QPS for runtime variants.

2026-03-05: Eng review (Rajiv) — recommended adding KV-cache warmup step before canary to avoid cold-latency spikes; increased planned canary duration from 15m to 45m for models with >2K context length. Action: update templates and add warmup checklist.
2026-03-07: SRE (Hannah) requested explicit circuit-breaker thresholds and prometheus alerting rules for canary windows. Added proposed alert set and escalation contacts.

2026-03-08: Decided trade-off between faster ramp (shorter waves) vs cost: settled on conservative default waves but document a fast-path template for low-risk infra-only config using feature flag gate.

2026-03-10: Internal dry-run scheduled in staging for 2026-03-22 to validate telemetry, rollback automation, and communications flow. Need Eng to provide routing-policy API change by 2026-03-18 (see dependencies).
